newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico rights group denounces attacks on reporters.
newsitem.headline: Mexico rights group denounces attacks on reporters.

text.p: A Mexican human rights group on Friday denounced a series of recent attacks on journalists by what it said could be shadowy government security forces.

The recent attacks on several Mexican journalists could be seen as an effort by the Mexican government to clamp down on freedom of expression, said the left-wing Miguel Agustin Pro Juarez Human Rights Centre in a statement.

Freelancer Jesus Ramirez, who works for Reuters, and two other journalists, Mauricio Laguna and Martin Reyes, were held for several hours by a group of armed men on October 12 in Mexico City shortly after covering an anti-government protest march.

Ramirez said the armed men claimed to have recognised the three as journalists and wanted to carry out a routine security check on them. The journalists were taken to Mexico City's subway, held for two hours and threatened with death, Ramirez said, adding that they were then robbed of their belongings.

"The aggression against (them), by an unidentified group with para-police characteristics that acts covertly and with impunity, is a worrisome reminder of the 1970s dirty war in our country and of similar groups in Central America known as death squads," the Miguel Agustin Pro Juarez group said.
Government officials could not be reached for comment, but in similar cases in the past have vigorously denied any official involvement in the abduction of journalists.
Ramirez has worked for several years as a journalist, most recently covering the Zapatista rebellion in southern Chiapas state.
